search_strategy: Thorough and iterative, chat-only (correctly, since all 47 g11 remarks live in Mattermost). Sequence: (1) Mattermost API login + team/channel list; (2) a single narrow keyword search ('ledger','tinker') that hit several remarks immediately by luck; (3) dumped the ENTIRE Mattermost corpus (~10k posts, 12 channels) to /tmp/mm/posts.json; (4) wrote and iterated a keyword-substring search script (/tmp/s.py) — first exact substrings ('CHECKPOINT_REASONS','decay warmup cosine learning rate','min_lr_ratio'), catching most of the June-2 reversal and the herrings; (5) read specific channel index ranges with /tmp/c.py (engineering 1590-1660, help 78-140, code-review 1890-1935/2930-2960) once threads were located; (6) built three successively tighter keyword-filter dumps (filt.py -> filt2.py -> filt3.py, the last with word-boundary regex to kill false positives like 'lr' inside 'already') producing /tmp/ft.txt/ft2.txt/ft3.txt (243-533 messages), then paged them via 'sed -n' / terminal screen, hand-assembling clustered ranges into /tmp/ctx.txt; (7) separately dumped and grepped all 228 wiki pages (fetched whole, since BookStack comments aren't search-indexed) and all 107 mail messages — both correctly came up empty for finetuning content, which the agent noted rather than treating as a search failure; (8) checked Gitea issues/PR bodies+comments, also empty of ledger-specific design. The main loss mechanism was NOT missed searches but never doing full sequential channel reads of #pipeline, #incidents, #general, #viewer, #releases, #cookbooks (only #engineering, #code-review and #help got full-range c.py reads) — several remarks (l9, l11, l13, l14, l19, r2.l9, r2.l11, r2.l14, r2.l15, r2.say19) sat in those channels outside any keyword net and were never seen. Two accidents also cost some fidelity: an early filt.py used printf with '\\n' which wrote literal backslash-n into the file (caught and fixed after one wasted read, line 2971), and the terminal-screen viewport repeatedly truncated large dumps to their last ~50-90 lines, likely why r2.l3's settling answer (dario, 'sitting on base_lr... not one step later') and the numeric half of say24 were in a dump the agent generated but never actually read.
end_reason: Run completed normally: task_complete=true, 145/145 tests passing (finetune suite + full repo), ruff clean, branch pushed, PR opened and merged to main (commit ec44913, PR #737), Gitea Actions CI green on the merge commit, and the agent explicitly re-verified the CI run on the main HEAD before declaring done (line 9322-9329). All 9 declared facts scored 1; reward 1.
notable: v11 rewrote g11.r2.rev2 (konrad, #general, 2025-06-02 10:16) to add the decay-floor half ('the end doesnt sit at zero any more, it bottoms out at a tenth of base_lr and holds there, and a first step at rate 0 is not something i want to keep defending'). This run's world served exactly that NEW wording, verbatim, twice — once in the s.py search dump (transcript line 2599-2602) and again in the full #general channel context (line 2637-2640). The answer key on disk still quotes only the OLD, warmup-only wording ('right. we had it that decay lands at exactly zero at total_steps and warmup keeps the strict step < warmup_steps compare tinker_trainer already uses. thats the bit thats going.'). Grading this run against what the world actually served (not the stale key text) is correct, and this run's shipped code (MIN_LR_RATIO=0.1 floor, 1<=step<=effective_warmup, effective_warmup=min(warmup_steps,total_steps), clipped not raising) matches the rewritten rev2 exactly.

This run saw BOTH r2 herrings in full (dario's zero-decay 'settled' claim, incidents Jan-30, line 3383-3392; konrad's strict-compare confirmation, viewer Feb-19, line 3401-3414) and BOTH r2 reversals in full, and correctly implemented the reversed behavior — no herring-following anywhere in the shipped LR code.

This run never read either r1 herring's own turns (#releases Jan-21 dario 'both of them, we dont collapse it into something clever'; #releases Jan-28 emil 'two records, sorted alphabetically'). It only encountered the herrings' CONTENT secondhand, restated inside their own reversals (rev1 at line 4036, rev2 at line 3729, both dario/emil/konrad recapping 'we agreed X, that's gone now'). The facts still scored 1 because the reversal turns state the final rule completely on their own — the original herring text was never load-bearing for this run.

Six clue-only remarks were never located at all (l9, l11, l13, l14, l19 for r1; r2.l9, r2.l11, r2.l14, r2.l15, r2.say19 for r2 — ten total), all sitting in #pipeline, #incidents, #general, #viewer or #releases, which never got a full sequential c.py read. None of these cost a fact: each had a same-fact sibling remark (or the ticket text itself) that the agent did find, so the requirement was still reconstructed correctly, just from a narrower evidence base than the plant intended.

r2.l3 (dario, 'already the top... sitting on base_lr... not one step later') was only half-seen: konrad's opening question surfaced via keyword search (line 2588) but dario's settling answer never appeared in any dump the agent actually read.
